stem.text: Cars pass a checkpoint at a rate of C(t) cars per minute, where C is differentiable and t is measured in minutes. Measured values are C(0) = 15, C(10) = 22, C(20) = 18, C(30) = 12. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{30} C(t)\,dt \), the number of cars that pass the checkpoint from t = 0 to t = 30, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 10 \cdot \frac{15 + 22}{2} = 185 \); \( 10 \cdot \frac{22 + 18}{2} = 200 \); \( 10 \cdot \frac{18 + 12}{2} = 150 \).

distractor_derivations.A: right Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
distractor_derivations.C: factor 1/2 applied to the first trapezoid only
distractor_derivations.D: left Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
